briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Crowns Its Best Buds While National Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis scene keeps finding bright spots — from Zalympix gold medals to a new Ypsilanti storefront and a gubernatorial candidate courting industry dollars with a tax-repeal pledge — even as regulators tighten enforcement and the wholesale tax fight rolls on. Nationally, psychedelics had a banner week with a well-received FDA hearing and fresh NDA momentum, while cannabis rescheduling hit a procedural pause rather than a real setback.

local.text: Mitten Canna Co. and Hytek crowned at Zalympix 2026 — Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom and Hytek's Oishii Piña took the top flower and rosin prizes at Michigan's 'Grammys of Cannabis.'
Bloom City Club expands footprint into Ypsilanti — the Ann Arbor-rooted retailer opened a new Ypsilanti dispensary and is running cannabis-themed events through October to celebrate.

Gubernatorial hopeful courts industry with tax-repeal vow — Michigan's top cannabis executives have thrown roughly $90,000 behind GOP candidate John James after he pledged to repeal the state's 24% wholesale tax.

Michigan still the Midwest's best deal on flower — the average ounce runs about $60 here versus $150–$220 in Ohio and Illinois, pulling in cross-border shoppers and pushing small border-town stores past Detroit in sales.

CRA enforcement protects legit operators from bad actors — regulators handed out back-to-back record-tying $2 million fines, including one against a grower caught shipping dirt and mulch labeled as marijuana flower.

national.text: FDA's psychedelic hearing draws upbeat reviews — speakers at a late-September FDA hearing on psychedelic therapy were described as overwhelmingly positive, with business owners, therapists and researchers outlining real progress on access and training.

Compass and Definium gear up for approval filings — with Lykos' 2024 rejection in the rearview, Compass Pathways and Definium Therapeutics are leading what one analyst calls a potentially huge year for the psychedelics field.

FDA publishes new regulatory framework for psychedelics — the agency's framework, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, reshapes trial design and access rules for psilocybin and MDMA therapies going forward.

Curaleaf pushes cross-border consolidation with Aurora bid — Curaleaf launched a $4-per-share takeover offer for Aurora Cannabis, a 45% premium that would create a combined company with $1.5 billion-plus in pro forma revenue.

DEA rescheduling hits a procedural pause, not a reversal — a DEA judge stayed the marijuana rescheduling hearing to weigh a new GAO report, but April's separate medical-cannabis order remains unaffected and the government must respond by Oct. 13.
